paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss Ratio FLOPs
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the loss ratio as a function of TFLOPs for five different model configurations, comparing their performance across a range of computational budgets. The x-axis, labeled "TFLOPs", is on a logarithmic scale, spanning from 1e7 to 9e8, with tick marks at intervals of one order of magnitude. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Ratio (%)", ranges from 94% to 100% and is presented on a linear scale. The plot includes five distinct lines: a purple line with triangle markers representing "Vanilla"; an orange line with circle markers for "SepLLM (n=64)"; a blue line with cross markers for "SepLLM (n=128)"; a green line with diamond markers for "SepLLM (n=64, H)"; and a red line with circle markers for "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)". The "Vanilla" model maintains a constant loss ratio of 100% across the entire TFLOPs range. The "SepLLM (n=64)" model starts at a loss ratio of approximately 98.3% at 1e7 TFLOPs and increases to a peak of approximately 100% at 4e8 TFLOPs before slightly declining. The "SepLLM (n=128)" model begins at a loss ratio of approximately 97% at 1e7 TFLOPs and rises to a peak of approximately 100% at 6e8 TFLOPs, remaining above 99.5% for the rest of the range. The "SepLLM (n=64, H)" model starts at a loss ratio of approximately 97.5% at 1e7 TFLOPs and increases to a peak of approximately 100% at 6e8 TFLOPs. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" model begins at a loss ratio of 94% at 1e7 TFLOPs and steadily increases to a peak of approximately 99.3% at 3e8 TFLOPs, after which it plateaus near 99% for the remainder of the range.
